audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags the level chart as contradicting the data: Teemo wins 53.75% over 1453 games, but content.win gives Zaahen four of seven stages and Teemo zero. The full layer's phases give Teemo four stages and Zaahen zero, so the two layers also contradict each other outright.
audit.why: A reader who opens the level chart is told he loses a lane he statistically wins, and the two views of the same matchup disagree. The stages that are genuinely Teemo's are the ranged-versus-melee ones: at level 1 Zaahen's only tool is The Darkin Glaive, a melee-range empowered auto, and at 4-5 the entry's own text says shrooms and poke zone his approaches and calls it 'your safest farming window'.
audit.corrected: Level 1 and Levels 4-5 belong to Teemo. Level 6 stays a wash, and the item stages stay Zaahen's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Neither layer contains a single number, and the full layer refers to his abilities only as 'Ultimate' and 'his big cooldown'.
audit.why: Aureate Rush is 10s at rank 1 falling to 8s, The Darkin Glaive is 10s to 6s, Dreaded Return is 14s to 12s, Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, which means your dart out-cycles his gap-closer at every rank of it — that is the whole reason a 53.75% number exists, and it was nowhere in the entry.
audit.corrected: Aureate Rush 10s->8s vs your flat 7s dart; hold the dart for his dash rather than spending it on chip.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names a single Zaahen ability — tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, breakdown.mid and breakdown.spikes all say 'Ultimate' as a placeholder.
audit.why: His ultimate is Grim Deliverance and the ability that actually decides the lane is Aureate Rush (E). Naming them is the difference between advice a player can act on and a template.
audit.corrected: Q The Darkin Glaive, W Dreaded Return, E Aureate Rush, R Grim Deliverance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says what The Darkin Glaive actually is.
audit.why: It is an auto-attack reset that heals him and can be recast for a knock-up on the following attack — the missing-interactions file flags both the auto-reset tell and the anti-heal need. The wind-up is the cue to step back, and Grievous Wounds is what makes your poison stick against it and against Grim Deliverance.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive is an auto reset that heals; the wind-up is the tell, and anti-heal answers it and the R together.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours as shrooms and poke zone his approaches — bank that safety, because both item stages after are his: durability and passive sustain shrug off your chip even through the blind. Wait for Aureate Rush before you step up, shove from range, and convert the lane into map control.

notes: IMPORTANT — the level-chart fix is only half-applicable under the fixed-length rule. content.win[1], win[2], win[5] and win[6] all read 'Zaahen' (6 chars) and there is no 5-or-6 character replacement, so any de-escalation of those stages falls outside the +/-10% band and would be rejected by the applier. I proposed only win[0] and win[3] (both 'Skill' -> 'Teemo', same length). After those apply the chart reads Teemo 2 / Skill 1 / Zaahen 4, which is better but still does not match a 53.75% Teemo win rate — win[1] and win[2] need a manual edit to 'Skill' outside the length rule. The full layer's phases already give Teemo four stages, so the two layers disagreed before this proposal and will still partly disagree after it.
